# resend_webhook (Data Source)

Looks up an existing Resend webhook by ID. The HMAC `signing_secret` is returned by Resend's GET endpoint, so importing-then-reading is a viable adoption path.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.5"

  required_providers {
    resend = {
      source  = "armaaar/resend"
      version = "~> 1.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "resend" {}

# Read an existing Resend webhook. The HMAC signing_secret is returned by
# Resend's GET endpoint — pipe it into your secret store on the consumer side
# so request verification stays in sync with the source of truth.
data "resend_webhook" "deliverability" {
  id = "wh_abc123"
}

output "webhook_signing_secret" {
  description = "HMAC signing secret for the deliverability webhook."
  value       = data.resend_webhook.deliverability.signing_secret
  sensitive   = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the webhook within Resend.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The date and time the webhook was created.
- `endpoint` (String) HTTPS URL Resend POSTs events to.
- `events` (List of String) Event types subscribed to.
- `signing_secret` (String, Sensitive) HMAC signing secret used to verify webhook requests. Sensitive credential material.
- `status` (String) Webhook status (`enabled` or `disabled`).
